WHMapper is written in C# with ASP.NET Core Blazor Server, EF Core and SignalR, and uses these components: Blazor.DIAGRAMS MudBlazor
We recommend using a domain name (your.domain.com) with public DNS for easy and consistent access.

WHMapper logs pilots in with CCP's SSO and reads their location through the ESI API. Register an application at developers.eveonline.com: Click the "MANAGE APPLICATIONS" button. Click the "CREATE NEW APPLICATION" button. Choose a name for your installation (e.g., prod eve-whmapper). Enter a description for this installation (e.g., WHMapper production). Change "CONNECTION TYPE" to "Authentication & API Access". Add the minimum required "PERMISSIONS" (scopes): esi-location.read_location.v1 esi-location.read_ship_type.v1 esi-ui.open_window.v1 esi-ui.write_waypoint.v1 esi-search.search_structures.v1 Set your "CALLBACK URL" (e.g., https://your.domain.com/sso/callback). Click the "CREATE APPLICATION" button. Copy the Client ID, Secret Key, and Callback URL for use in the next configuration step.

Install WHMapper with Docker (recommended), or directly on Linux or Windows with the pre-built binaries. Docker Self-Hosted (Binary) ⚠️ Beta Deploy with Docker & Compose The Docker install runs WHMapper, PostgreSQL, Redis and an HTTPS reverse proxy with Docker Compose. An init script asks for your settings and prepares everything. Server​ We recommend using a Linux server with the Debian OS for optimal performance and support. If you prefer to use a different operating system, you will need to write your own init script or manually configure the necessary files (see the list below). Docker​ Install Docker with Compose first: Linux (Docker Engine) Windows OS X Get the Compose files​ Navigate to your desired installation location. Clone the WHMapper repository (we recommend /opt/ on Linux). Linux sudo git clone https://github.com/pfh59/eve-whmapper.git cd eve-whmapper/deploy/docker Windows git clone https://github.com/pfh59/eve-whmapper.git cd eve-whmapper/deploy/docker Configuration​ Run the init script (as root on Linux, as Administrator on Windows) and answer its questions: Linux sudo ./init.sh Windows ./init.ps1 The script: writes your answers into docker-compose.yml, haproxy.cfg and nginx.conf; creates the Docker containers; gets a certificate for your domain, so WHMapper is served over HTTPS. Start and stop​ To manage the Docker containers, use the provided scripts: Linux To Start all containers: Use the start.sh script as a sudo or root user. sudo ./start.sh To Stop all containers: Use the stop.sh script as a sudo or root user. sudo ./stop.sh Windows To Start all containers: Use the start.ps1 script as an Administrator. ./start.ps1 To Stop all containers: Use the stop.ps1 script as an Administrator. ./stop.ps1 Self-Hosted Installation (Binary) This guide covers installing WHMapper directly on Linux Debian or Windows without Docker, using the pre-built binaries published on GitHub Releases. Beta — feedback welcome This self-hosted (binary) installation method is new and has had limited real-world testing compared to the Docker method. Steps may be incomplete or unclear for some environments (distributions, Windows versions, reverse proxy setups, etc.). If you run into an issue, a step that doesn't work, or anything unclear, please open an issue on the docs repository — your feedback directly helps fix and clarify this guide. Requirements​ Component Minimum version .NET ASP.NET Core Runtime 10.0 PostgreSQL 17 Redis 8 Architecture The published binaries are framework-dependent (not self-contained). The .NET 10 ASP.NET Core Runtime must be installed on the host — the .NET SDK is not required. Installation​ Linux (x64 / ARM) Windows (x64) 1. Install .NET 10 ASP.NET Core Runtime​ Follow the official Microsoft instructions for your distribution: https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/install/linux Debian example: # Add Microsoft package repository wget https://packages.microsoft.com/config/debian/12/packages-microsoft-prod.deb -O packages-microsoft-prod.deb sudo dpkg -i packages-microsoft-prod.deb rm packages-microsoft-prod.deb # Install the runtime (not the full SDK) sudo apt-get update sudo apt-get install -y aspnetcore-runtime-10.0 Verify: dotnet --info 2. Install PostgreSQL 17​ sudo apt-get install -y postgresql-17 sudo systemctl enable --now postgresql 3. Install Redis 8​ sudo apt-get install -y redis-server sudo systemctl enable --now redis-server 4. Create a system user​ sudo useradd --system --no-create-home --shell /usr/sbin/nologin whmapper 5. Download and extract the binary​ Download the latest release from GitHub Releases. # Create installation directory sudo mkdir -p /opt/whmapper sudo mkdir -p /opt/whmapper/Logs # Download the binary (replace vX.Y.Z with the actual version) wget https://github.com/pfh59/eve-whmapper/releases/download/vX.Y.Z/WHMapper.linux-x64.zip -O /tmp/WHMapper.linux-x64.zip # For ARM systems, use: # wget https://github.com/pfh59/eve-whmapper/releases/download/vX.Y.Z/WHMapper.linux-arm.zip -O /tmp/WHMapper.linux-arm.zip sudo unzip /tmp/WHMapper.linux-x64.zip -d /opt/whmapper sudo chown -R whmapper:whmapper /opt/whmapper sudo chmod +x /opt/whmapper/WHMapper 6. Configure PostgreSQL​ sudo -u postgres psql <<EOF CREATE USER whmapper WITH PASSWORD 'your_strong_password'; CREATE DATABASE whmapper OWNER whmapper; GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON DATABASE whmapper TO whmapper; EOF 7. Configure the application​ Create an environment file with your settings: sudo nano /etc/whmapper.env /etc/whmapper.env EveSSO__ClientId=your_ccp_client_id EveSSO__Secret=your_ccp_secret ConnectionStrings__DatabaseConnection=server=localhost;port=5432;database=whmapper;User Id=whmapper;Password=your_strong_password ConnectionStrings__RedisConnection=localhost:6379 Serilog__MinimumLevel__Default=Warning sudo chmod 600 /etc/whmapper.env sudo chown whmapper:whmapper /etc/whmapper.env 8. Create a systemd service​ sudo nano /etc/systemd/system/whmapper.service /etc/systemd/system/whmapper.service [Unit] Description=EVE Wormhole Mapper After=network.target postgresql.service redis-server.service Requires=postgresql.service redis-server.service [Service] Type=simple User=whmapper WorkingDirectory=/opt/whmapper ExecStart=/opt/whmapper/WHMapper EnvironmentFile=/etc/whmapper.env Restart=on-failure RestartSec=10 [Install] WantedBy=multi-user.target sudo systemctl daemon-reload sudo systemctl enable --now whmapper sudo systemctl status whmapper The application will start on port 5000 (HTTP) by default when run without a reverse proxy. 9. (Optional) Configure nginx as a reverse proxy with HTTPS​ sudo apt-get install -y nginx certbot python3-certbot-nginx /etc/nginx/sites-available/whmapper server { listen 80; server_name your.domain.com; location / { proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:5000; proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade; proxy_set_header Connection "upgrade"; proxy_set_header Host $host; proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme; proxy_cache_bypass $http_upgrade; } } sudo ln -s /etc/nginx/sites-available/whmapper /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/ sudo nginx -t sudo systemctl reload nginx # Obtain a Let's Encrypt certificate sudo certbot --nginx -d your.domain.com Add this variable to /etc/whmapper.env so that WHMapper only listens on localhost, behind nginx: ASPNETCORE_URLS=http://127.0.0.1:5000 Restart the service: sudo systemctl restart whmapper 1. Install .NET 10 ASP.NET Core Runtime​ Download and install the ASP.NET Core Runtime 10.0 from the official page: https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/10.0 Select "ASP.NET Core Runtime" (not the SDK). Verify in PowerShell: dotnet --info 2. Install PostgreSQL 17​ Download the Windows installer from www.enterprisedb.com/downloads/postgres-postgresql-downloads. During setup: Note the port (default: 5432) Set a strong password for the postgres superuser Alternatively, with Chocolatey: choco install postgresql17 --params '/Password:your_strong_password' 3. Install Redis​ Redis does not have an official Windows binary. Use Memurai (Redis-compatible for Windows): Download and install from www.memurai.com. It runs as a Windows service on port 6379 by default. Alternatively, use Redis on Windows via WSL2. 4. Download and extract the binary​ Download the latest release from GitHub Releases. # Create installation directory New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path "C:\whmapper" -Force New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path "C:\whmapper\Logs" -Force # Download (replace vX.Y.Z with the actual version) Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "https://github.com/pfh59/eve-whmapper/releases/download/vX.Y.Z/WHMapper.win-x64.zip" ` -OutFile "$env:TEMP\WHMapper.win-x64.zip" Expand-Archive -Path "$env:TEMP\WHMapper.win-x64.zip" -DestinationPath "C:\whmapper" -Force 5. Configure PostgreSQL​ Open pgAdmin or psql and run: CREATE USER whmapper WITH PASSWORD 'your_strong_password'; CREATE DATABASE whmapper OWNER whmapper; GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON DATABASE whmapper TO whmapper; Or via psql in PowerShell: & "C:\Program Files\PostgreSQL\17 in\psql.exe" -U postgres -c "CREATE USER whmapper WITH PASSWORD 'your_strong_password';" & "C:\Program Files\PostgreSQL\17 in\psql.exe" -U postgres -c "CREATE DATABASE whmapper OWNER whmapper;" 6. Configure the application​ Create a configuration file next to the binary: New-Item -Path "C:\whmapper\appsettings.Production.json" -ItemType File Edit C:\whmapper\appsettings.Production.json: C:\whmapper\appsettings.Production.json { "EveSSO": { "ClientId": "your_ccp_client_id", "Secret": "your_ccp_secret" }, "ConnectionStrings": { "DatabaseConnection": "server=localhost;port=5432;database=whmapper;User Id=whmapper;Password=your_strong_password", "RedisConnection": "localhost:6379" }, "Serilog": { "MinimumLevel": { "Default": "Warning" } } } Environment variables as alternative You can also configure the application using system environment variables instead of a file. Environment variable names use __ as separator (e.g., EveSSO__ClientId). 7. Register as a Windows Service​ Open PowerShell as Administrator: # Set the ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT so the Production config is loaded [System.Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT", "Production", "Machine") # Register the service sc.exe create "WHMapper" ` binPath= "C:\whmapper\WHMapper.exe" ` start= auto ` DisplayName= "EVE Wormhole Mapper" sc.exe description "WHMapper" "EVE Wormhole Mapper - self-hosted binary" # Start the service sc.exe start "WHMapper" Check the service status: sc.exe query "WHMapper" Logs are written to C:\whmapper\Logs\. 8. (Optional) Configure nginx as a reverse proxy with HTTPS​ Download nginx for Windows from nginx.org/en/download.html and extract it to C:
ginx. Edit C:
ginx\conf
ginx.conf: C:
ginx\conf
ginx.conf worker_processes 1; events { worker_connections 1024; } http { server { listen 80; server_name your.domain.com; location / { proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:5000; proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade; proxy_set_header Connection "upgrade"; proxy_set_header Host $host; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme; } } server { listen 443 ssl; server_name your.domain.com; ssl_certificate C:/nginx/certs/fullchain.pem; ssl_certificate_key C:/nginx/certs/privkey.pem; location / { proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:5000; proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade; proxy_set_header Connection "upgrade"; proxy_set_header Host $host; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto https; } } } Register nginx as a Windows service using NSSM: nssm install nginx "C:
ginx
ginx.exe" nssm start nginx Place your SSL certificates in C:
ginx\certs\. Make WHMapper listen on localhost only, behind nginx, by setting this system environment variable (PowerShell as Administrator): [System.Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("ASPNETCORE_URLS", "http://127.0.0.1:5000", "Machine") Restart the WHMapper service: sc.exe stop "WHMapper" sc.exe start "WHMapper" Configuration Reference​ Key Environment variable Default Description EveSSO.ClientId EveSSO__ClientId (none) CCP SSO Client ID EveSSO.Secret EveSSO__Secret (none) CCP SSO Secret ConnectionStrings.DatabaseConnection ConnectionStrings__DatabaseConnection (none) PostgreSQL connection string ConnectionStrings.RedisConnection ConnectionStrings__RedisConnection (none) Redis connection string — ASPNETCORE_URLS http://localhost:5000 Addresses and ports WHMapper listens on https_port https_port 443 Port used when redirecting HTTP requests to HTTPS Instances.SingleTenantMode Instances__SingleTenantMode false Allow only one instance on the deployment (see Single-Tenant Mode) DisableSignalRCertificateValidation DisableSignalRCertificateValidation false Disable TLS validation for SignalR (local/dev only) Serilog.MinimumLevel.Default Serilog__MinimumLevel__Default Warning Log level Updating​ To update to a newer version: Download the new binary from GitHub Releases. Stop the service. Replace the files in the installation directory (keep your appsettings.Production.json or environment file). Start the service. Database migrations are applied automatically on startup.

Download the latest release from GitHub Releases. # Create installation directory sudo mkdir -p /opt/whmapper sudo mkdir -p /opt/whmapper/Logs # Download the binary (replace vX.Y.Z with the actual version) wget https://github.com/pfh59/eve-whmapper/releases/download/vX.Y.Z/WHMapper.linux-x64.zip -O /tmp/WHMapper.linux-x64.zip # For ARM systems, use: # wget https://github.com/pfh59/eve-whmapper/releases/download/vX.Y.Z/WHMapper.linux-arm.zip -O /tmp/WHMapper.linux-arm.zip sudo unzip /tmp/WHMapper.linux-x64.zip -d /opt/whmapper sudo chown -R whmapper:whmapper /opt/whmapper sudo chmod +x /opt/whmapper/WHMapper
sudo -u postgres psql <<EOF CREATE USER whmapper WITH PASSWORD 'your_strong_password'; CREATE DATABASE whmapper OWNER whmapper; GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON DATABASE whmapper TO whmapper; EOF

Create an environment file with your settings: sudo nano /etc/whmapper.env /etc/whmapper.env EveSSO__ClientId=your_ccp_client_id EveSSO__Secret=your_ccp_secret ConnectionStrings__DatabaseConnection=server=localhost;port=5432;database=whmapper;User Id=whmapper;Password=your_strong_password ConnectionStrings__RedisConnection=localhost:6379 Serilog__MinimumLevel__Default=Warning sudo chmod 600 /etc/whmapper.env sudo chown whmapper:whmapper /etc/whmapper.env

sudo nano /etc/systemd/system/whmapper.service /etc/systemd/system/whmapper.service [Unit] Description=EVE Wormhole Mapper After=network.target postgresql.service redis-server.service Requires=postgresql.service redis-server.service [Service] Type=simple User=whmapper WorkingDirectory=/opt/whmapper ExecStart=/opt/whmapper/WHMapper EnvironmentFile=/etc/whmapper.env Restart=on-failure RestartSec=10 [Install] WantedBy=multi-user.target sudo systemctl daemon-reload sudo systemctl enable --now whmapper sudo systemctl status whmapper The application will start on port 5000 (HTTP) by default when run without a reverse proxy.

sudo apt-get install -y nginx certbot python3-certbot-nginx /etc/nginx/sites-available/whmapper server { listen 80; server_name your.domain.com; location / { proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:5000; proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade; proxy_set_header Connection "upgrade"; proxy_set_header Host $host; proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme; proxy_cache_bypass $http_upgrade; } } sudo ln -s /etc/nginx/sites-available/whmapper /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/ sudo nginx -t sudo systemctl reload nginx # Obtain a Let's Encrypt certificate sudo certbot --nginx -d your.domain.com Add this variable to /etc/whmapper.env so that WHMapper only listens on localhost, behind nginx: ASPNETCORE_URLS=http://127.0.0.1:5000 Restart the service: sudo systemctl restart whmapper

documents.t: Download and install the ASP.NET Core Runtime 10.0 from the official page: https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/10.0 Select "ASP.NET Core Runtime" (not the SDK). Verify in PowerShell: dotnet --info

Download the Windows installer from www.enterprisedb.com/downloads/postgres-postgresql-downloads. During setup: Note the port (default: 5432) Set a strong password for the postgres superuser Alternatively, with Chocolatey: choco install postgresql17 --params '/Password:your_strong_password'

Redis does not have an official Windows binary. Use Memurai (Redis-compatible for Windows): Download and install from www.memurai.com. It runs as a Windows service on port 6379 by default. Alternatively, use Redis on Windows via WSL2.

Download the latest release from GitHub Releases. # Create installation directory New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path "C:\whmapper" -Force New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path "C:\whmapper\Logs" -Force # Download (replace vX.Y.Z with the actual version) Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "https://github.com/pfh59/eve-whmapper/releases/download/vX.Y.Z/WHMapper.win-x64.zip" ` -OutFile "$env:TEMP\WHMapper.win-x64.zip" Expand-Archive -Path "$env:TEMP\WHMapper.win-x64.zip" -DestinationPath "C:\whmapper" -Force

Open pgAdmin or psql and run: CREATE USER whmapper WITH PASSWORD 'your_strong_password'; CREATE DATABASE whmapper OWNER whmapper; GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON DATABASE whmapper TO whmapper; Or via psql in PowerShell: & "C:\Program Files\PostgreSQL\17\bin\psql.exe" -U postgres -c "CREATE USER whmapper WITH PASSWORD 'your_strong_password';" & "C:\Program Files\PostgreSQL\17\bin\psql.exe" -U postgres -c "CREATE DATABASE whmapper OWNER whmapper;"

Create a configuration file next to the binary: New-Item -Path "C:\whmapper\appsettings.Production.json" -ItemType File Edit C:\whmapper\appsettings.Production.json: C:\whmapper\appsettings.Production.json { "EveSSO": { "ClientId": "your_ccp_client_id", "Secret": "your_ccp_secret" }, "ConnectionStrings": { "DatabaseConnection": "server=localhost;port=5432;database=whmapper;User Id=whmapper;Password=your_strong_password", "RedisConnection": "localhost:6379" }, "Serilog": { "MinimumLevel": { "Default": "Warning" } } } Environment variables as alternative You can also configure the application using system environment variables instead of a file. Environment variable names use __ as separator (e.g., EveSSO__ClientId).

Open PowerShell as Administrator: # Set the ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT so the Production config is loaded [System.Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT", "Production", "Machine") # Register the service sc.exe create "WHMapper" ` binPath= "C:\whmapper\WHMapper.exe" ` start= auto ` DisplayName= "EVE Wormhole Mapper" sc.exe description "WHMapper" "EVE Wormhole Mapper - self-hosted binary" # Start the service sc.exe start "WHMapper" Check the service status: sc.exe query "WHMapper" Logs are written to C:\whmapper\Logs\.

Download nginx for Windows from nginx.org/en/download.html and extract it to C:
ginx. Edit C:
ginx\conf
ginx.conf: C:
ginx\conf
ginx.conf worker_processes 1; events { worker_connections 1024; } http { server { listen 80; server_name your.domain.com; location / { proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:5000; proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade; proxy_set_header Connection "upgrade"; proxy_set_header Host $host; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme; } } server { listen 443 ssl; server_name your.domain.com; ssl_certificate C:/nginx/certs/fullchain.pem; ssl_certificate_key C:/nginx/certs/privkey.pem; location / { proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:5000; proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade; proxy_set_header Connection "upgrade"; proxy_set_header Host $host; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto https; } } } Register nginx as a Windows service using NSSM: nssm install nginx "C:
ginx
ginx.exe" nssm start nginx Place your SSL certificates in C:
ginx\certs\. Make WHMapper listen on localhost only, behind nginx, by setting this system environment variable (PowerShell as Administrator): [System.Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("ASPNETCORE_URLS", "http://127.0.0.1:5000", "Machine") Restart the WHMapper service: sc.exe stop "WHMapper" sc.exe start "WHMapper"

To update to a newer version: Download the new binary from GitHub Releases. Stop the service. Replace the files in the installation directory (keep your appsettings.Production.json or environment file). Start the service. Database migrations are applied automatically on startup.
Ask on the GitHub repository or on the EVE Online forum thread. Next step → First Start
On first start, EVE Wormhole Mapper prepares its database and the EVE static data it needs. Both steps are automatic — no action is required.

info Database: the PostgreSQL schema is created, or migrated to the new version, every time the application starts. Static data (SDE): the first time the home page is opened, WHMapper downloads and installs the EVE Static Data Export (SDE). This happens again only if the SDE is missing, for example after its files were removed. The SDE installation shows the following steps: Remove Current SDE Package (1/4): The existing Static Data Export (SDE) package is removed to ensure no outdated data interferes with the new setup. Download SDE Package (2/4): The latest SDE package is downloaded. This package contains critical game data required for accurate wormhole mapping. Extract SDE Package (3/4): The downloaded package is extracted, preparing the data for use. Initialize SDE Cache (4/4): The system initializes the SDE cache, optimizing performance and ensuring all data is readily accessible. Once these steps are completed, the main page is displayed and the application is ready for use.
For the first login, you need to authenticate your account. Refer to the Authentication Module for detailed instructions. Next step → Authentication
WHMapper uses your EVE Online account through CCP's Single Sign-On (SSO). Your password is never sent to WHMapper — only a token issued by CCP is stored.

Open the account menu — click Account at the top-right of the home page. Initiate Login — click Login to be redirected to the CCP SSO page. Enter CCP Credentials — input your CCP username and password. Select a Character — choose which character to use. Authorize Scopes — review and approve the required access rights.

Once CCP has authenticated you, WHMapper checks which instances you can access: You belong to an instance — the first accessible map loads automatically. You don't belong to any instance — the No Instance Access screen is shown. You can create your own instance or ask an administrator to grant you access. Refer to the Instance page for the full walkthrough.

You can link several EVE characters to the same session using the Add Account button. Each linked character appears as a badge in the top bar. The primary character — used for all mapper actions and access checks — is highlighted with a white circle. To change the primary character, right-click another character's badge and choose Set as Primary. The maps you can open follow the access rights of the primary character. The same menu enables or disables location tracking for each character (see Map → Pilot Tracking). Next step → Instance Setup

An instance is your isolated WHMapper environment. It groups maps, administrators, and access rules under a single owner (a character, corporation, or alliance). Every user who wants to use WHMapper must belong to at least one instance — either by creating their own or by being granted access to an existing one.

When you log in for the first time and your character, corporation, or alliance has not yet been granted access to any instance, WHMapper shows the following screen: From here you can either: Create an instance — become the administrator of your own environment. Ask an instance administrator to grant you access.

Click CREATE AN INSTANCE to open the registration dialog. Fill in the fields: Field Required Description Instance Name Yes A friendly name (e.g. My Corp Mapper). Description No An optional description of the instance. Instance Access Type Yes Defines who owns the instance — see below.

The access type determines the owner entity of the instance. The dropdown lists all entities linked to your authenticated character: Option Meaning Personal (Just me) The instance is owned by your character. Corporation The instance is owned by your corporation. Alliance The instance is owned by your alliance. Once the form is valid, click CREATE INSTANCE. You become the administrator of the new instance. What you get as creator Your own isolated mapping environment Full admin control over maps and access Ability to create and manage multiple maps Per-map access control to restrict who can see each map Ability to add other administrators Control over who can access your instance

Immediately after creating an instance, WHMapper has no map to display yet. You will see: This is expected — you need to add at least one map to your instance before the mapper becomes usable. See Add a map below.

Access your instances at any time via the user menu: Click My Instances to open the My Instances dialog. It lists every instance you belong to: Each entry shows: The instance name and owner character The description The number of maps and administrators A MANAGE link (visible only to administrators) To create another instance from this dialog, click + CREATE NEW INSTANCE.

Click MANAGE on any instance you administer to open the Instance Administration dialog: The dialog has three sections: Section Description Maps Maps belonging to this instance. Admins Users with administrator rights on this instance. Access Control Characters, corporations, or alliances granted access. At the top you can EDIT the instance name/description or DELETE the instance entirely. warning Only administrators of an instance can see the MANAGE option and open this dialog.

The Access Control section defines who can access the instance. By default, only the creator's character is listed. To grant access to a new entity, click + ADD ACCESS: Search by character name, corporation name, or alliance name. Select the result and click GRANT ACCESS. A confirmation toast appears: Connected pilots who gain access receive a notification that new maps are available. tip When access is granted to a corporation or alliance, all members of that entity gain access to the instance. Individual character entries can be used for finer-grained control. To revoke access, click the delete icon on the corresponding row.

In the Admins section, click + ADD to promote another character to administrator. Administrators can manage maps, access control, and instance settings. The creator of the instance always appears as Owner and cannot be removed from the admin list.
Click EDIT in the Instance Administration dialog to modify the instance name or description: Click SAVE to apply the changes or CANCEL to discard them.

In the Maps section, click + ADD. The Add Map dialog appears: Type a name for the map. The CREATE button becomes active once a name is entered: Click CREATE. The map is added to the instance: You can repeat this process to add as many maps as needed. To add a second map, click + ADD again, enter the new name, and click CREATE:

An instance can contain multiple maps. All users with access to the instance can view all maps by default. Each map appears as its own tab in the mapper interface, allowing users to switch between maps without leaving the application: The Maps section of the Instance Administration dialog displays the total number of maps and lists each one with its action buttons: A padlock badge on a map entry indicates that access restrictions have been applied to that map (the number shows how many access entries are configured). Tracking only updates the active map Pilot tracking adds systems and connections only to the active map — the tab currently selected in the mapper. Make sure all scouts use the same map tab.
Each map can have its own access restrictions, independent of the instance-level access control. By default, every user with access to the instance can view every map.

In the Maps section of the Instance Administration dialog, each map row shows two icons on the right: Blue shield icon — opens the Map Access Control dialog for that map. Red trash icon — deletes the map. Hovering over each icon shows its tooltip:

When no access entries have been added, the dialog shows a blue No restrictions banner: No restrictions: All users with instance access can view this map. Add an access entry below to restrict who can access this map. The lower section lists all entities that currently have instance-level access. Click + ADD next to any entry to restrict the map to that entity.

Once at least one access entry is added, the dialog switches to a yellow Restricted access banner: Restricted access: Only the entities listed below can access this map. Instance administrators always have access. Column Description Type Whether the entry is a Character, Corporation, or Alliance. Entity Name The name of the entity granted access. Actions Red trash icon to remove the entry. To remove all restrictions at once and make the map public to the instance again, click the REMOVE ALL RESTRICTIONS (MAKE PUBLIC TO INSTANCE) button. Instance admins always have access Regardless of per-map restrictions, instance administrators always retain access to all maps in their instance.

By default, WHMapper allows multiple instances to be created by any user. Single-Tenant Mode restricts this so that only one instance can exist across the entire deployment — once an instance is created, the CREATE AN INSTANCE option is locked for all other users. This is intended for self-hosted deployments where a single corporation or alliance owns the server and should be the sole instance owner. To enable single-tenant mode, set the following environment variable (Docker docker-compose.yml, or /etc/whmapper.env for the binary install): Instances__SingleTenantMode=True When this mode is active and an instance already exists, users who do not have access to that instance will see the standard No access screen without the option to create a new instance.

A user can belong to multiple instances simultaneously — either as a direct member, through their corporation, or through their alliance. In that case, WHMapper aggregates all maps from all accessible instances and displays them as tabs in a single view. The maps visible to you depend on two levels of rules: Instance-level access — you must be granted access to the instance. Per-map access — if a map has restrictions configured, only the listed entities can open it, even if they have instance access. Instance administrators always retain full access to all maps in their own instance, regardless of per-map restrictions. Next step → Using the Map

WHMapper records every jump through a connection: who jumped, when, and in which ship. With the connection's status and size, the jump log helps you judge how much mass a wormhole has left before you send more ships through.

Select a connection on the map to open the Connection window (see Map panels). The left side summarizes the connection: Field Description Size Size of the wormhole: Small, Medium, Large or XLarge Status Current status of the wormhole (see Wormhole status) First Jump Date, time, character and ship of the first recorded jump Last Jump Date, time, character and ship of the most recent jump The right side lists every recorded jump: Column Description Date Date of the jump (EVE time) Time Time of the jump (EVE time) Character Character who jumped Ship Ship used, or No ship used if the connection was created manually

When a tracked character jumps through a wormhole, WHMapper records the jump with the ship flown at that moment (see Pilot tracking). Every jump through the same connection is added to the log, and First Jump / Last Jump are updated (see the two jumps in the first screenshot).
When you create a connection by hand on the map, no ship is recorded: the log shows No ship used.

Status shows the mass status of the wormhole. When the wormhole is at end of life, its EOL status is shown next to it. Both are set from the connection menu on the map (see Editing a connection). Status Colour Meaning Normal Green Mass not reduced Reduced Orange Mass reduced: a large ship or several ships went through Verge Red About to collapse EOL -4h Purple End of life, less than about 4 hours left EOL -1h Purple End of life, less than about 1 hour left Mass status Normal with EOL -4h: Mass status Verge:

The map shows your wormhole chain: the systems you have found and the connections between them, through wormholes or stargates. Every change is synchronized live, so all pilots on the same map see the same chain at the same time. From the map you can: track where your characters are and let WHMapper add the systems they enter; add, move, lock, tag and delete systems; set the status, size and end of life of each connection; open the System, Notes, Signatures, Routes and Connection windows for the selected item. Who can open a map is set per instance and per map (see Instance).

The top bar shows how many pilots are currently on the active map tab. The count updates live as pilots join, leave or switch tabs. tip The count only covers the active tab. Make sure your fleet uses the same map tab to get an accurate number.

When tracking is on, WHMapper follows each of your characters through ESI: the system a character enters is added to the active map; the connection between the previous and the new system is created automatically; the character's name appears on the system it is in. After you log in, tracking is on for every character. A green dot on a character badge means tracking is on:

Right-click a character badge in the top bar: UnTrack turns tracking off for that character (red dot): Track turns it back on (green dot): Tracking only works on maps the character can open. When a character has no access to the active map, its badge shows a red dot and the menu shows No Map Access:

When several systems of the same class are connected to the same origin, WHMapper gives them sequential letters (A, B, C…). Use these letters to name your in-game bookmarks. To change a tag, select the system and press (default bindings, see Settings → Keyboard): Numpad + or Arrow Up: next letter (A → B); Numpad - or Arrow Down: previous letter (B → A). Bookmark examples: Bookmark Meaning >> LS - EJC Low-security exit >> LSB - KWE Second low-security exit from the same origin >> HS - MCE High-security exit
A selected system or connection is highlighted, and the windows for it open over the map (see Map panels).
Left-click a system. These windows open: System and Notes — see System Information; Signatures — see Signature; Routes — see Route Planner.
Left-click a connection. The Connection window replaces the system windows. It shows the connection's size, status and jump log (see Jump).

Ctrl + left-click adds a system to the selection, or removes it if it is already selected. This can be turned off in Settings → Mouse / Zoom. Shift + left-click and drag draws a selection area. Every system inside it is selected:

The System, Notes, Signatures, Routes and Connection windows float over the map. The map stays usable around them: clicks, right-clicks and zoom outside a window reach the map. System, Notes, Signatures and Routes follow the selected system. By default, System and Notes are top-right, Signatures bottom-left and Routes bottom-right. Connection follows the selected connection and replaces the system windows while a connection is selected.
Drag a window by its title bar. The window comes to the front when you press or move it, and always stays inside the map.
Each title bar has two buttons: the collapse arrow reduces the window to its title bar, or expands it again; Close (×) hides the window.

The dock at the top-left of the map shows or hides each window. A highlighted icon means the window is shown. A window that does not apply to the current selection has a disabled button. Hover it to see why: The last button, Reset panel layout, puts every window back in its default place, visible and expanded.
Drag the grip in the bottom-right corner of the Signatures window to resize it. It keeps a minimum size and stays inside the map. Long lists scroll inside their window.

When you clear the selection, for example by clicking an empty area of the map, the windows keep showing the last selected system or connection, dimmed. The title bar shows the system name, so you always know what is displayed.

Position, size, visibility and collapsed state are saved per map, in your browser, and restored when you reload the page. Each pilot can arrange the windows to fit their screen; the layout is not shared with other users or devices.

One system: drag it to its new position. Several systems: select them (see Selecting multiple systems), then drag any of them to move the whole group. Locked systems cannot be moved (see Lock a system).

Systems are added automatically by pilot tracking. To add one manually: Right-click an empty area of the map and choose Add System. Type at least three characters of the system name. Choose the system in the list (here, Amamake), then click ADD SYSTEM. A notification confirms that the system was added.
Right-click a system to open its menu.
Set Destination sets the system as your autopilot destination in the game.
Lock protects a system: it can no longer be moved or deleted. A padlock appears on the system. To remove the protection, choose UnLock in the same menu.

System Status marks what you know about a system. The status is shown by the border colour of the system. Status Meaning Appearance Unknown No information about this system Occupied Occupied by potential enemies Hostile Enemies present Friendly Allies present Empty Nobody in the system
Right-click a connection to open its menu.

EOL Status sets how long the wormhole has left before it collapses. EOL status Meaning Appearance Normal Not at end of life EOL -4h About 4 hours left (dashed purple) EOL -1h About 1 hour left (solid purple)
Status sets how much mass the wormhole has left. Status Meaning Appearance Normal Mass not reduced Reduced Mass reduced Verge About to collapse
Size sets the largest ship class that can jump through the wormhole. Size Appearance Small Medium Large (default) XLarge

Select the system, or several systems (see Selecting multiple systems). Press Delete. warning There is no confirmation: check your selection before pressing Delete. A locked system cannot be deleted. WHMapper shows a warning instead:

The Routes window counts how many jumps separate the selected system from your key destinations (trade hubs, home, staging…). It uses stargates and the wormholes on your map, and can also use Thera and Turnur connections. The window opens over the map when you select a system (see Map panels). Jump counts are recalculated each time you select another system.

Route type Connections used Custom (default) Stargates and the wormholes mapped in WHMapper Thera Custom, plus the current Thera connections Turnur Custom, plus the current Turnur connections Preference Effect Shorter (default) Fewest jumps Safer Prefers high-sec, even if the route is longer Example from J165153 with Thera, Shorter then Safer: info Thera and Turnur connections change during the day, so their jump counts change too.

There are two kinds of destinations: Global destinations are set by instance administrators and shown to everyone who can open the map; personal destinations are your own, added on top of the global ones. The buttons next to Route depend on your role: Button Action Who Add a global new route Administrators Add my new route Everyone Edit a route Administrators, and pilots who have personal destinations Administrator view: Pilot view: Multiple characters Personal destinations are recorded under your primary character, whichever character is active (see Authenticate → Multiple characters).

Click Add a global new route (administrators) or Add my new route. Type at least three characters of the system name, for example Jita: Choose the system, then click ADD SYSTEM (or CANCEL to close). The destination is added with its jump count from the selected system:

Click Edit a route . A trash icon appears next to each destination you can remove: administrators can remove global and personal destinations: pilots can remove their own personal destinations: Click the trash icon next to the destination. Click DELETE to confirm.

When a route exists, the number of jumps is shown next to the destination, with a green target icon. A route can go through mapped wormholes, stargates, and Thera or Turnur connections when that route type is selected. From a wormhole (J165153): From known space (Jita): When no route is found, the count shows 0 in red and the target icon is greyed out. This happens when the selected system, or the destination, is not connected to the rest of your map.

Click the target icon next to a destination to highlight its route on the map, in yellow. Click it again to hide the route. Show the route Hide the route note Only systems that are on your map are highlighted. Known-space jumps that are not mapped are part of the route, but are not drawn.
documents.s: Show a route on the map

documents.t: Hover the jump count of a destination to see the whole route as a row of dots, one per system, coloured by security status. Hover a dot to see the system name.
documents.s: See every system of a route

documents.t: Settings lets you adapt WHMapper to the way you play. You can configure keyboard shortcuts, mouse and zoom options, and map layout parameters. Once saved, these settings are automatically applied every time your primary character connects — you never need to reconfigure them between sessions.
Open the user menu (⋮ at the top-right of the screen) and click Settings. The Settings dialog opens with three tabs: KEYBOARD, MOUSE / ZOOM, and MAP.
The KEYBOARD tab lets you rebind the default keyboard shortcuts used on the map. tip Click a field, then press the key you want to use.

Action Default Key Description Link Systems L Manually create a connection between two selected systems Delete Delete Delete the selected system or connection Increment Extension NumpadAdd Increase the tag extension counter Decrement Extension NumpadSubtract Decrease the tag extension counter Increment Extension (Alt) ArrowUp Alternative key to increase the tag extension counter Decrement Extension (Alt) ArrowDown Alternative key to decrease the tag extension counter
The MOUSE / ZOOM tab controls mouse interaction and zoom behavior on the map.

Option Default Description Zoom Enabled ON Enables mouse-wheel zoom on the map canvas Inverse Zoom Direction OFF Reverses the zoom scroll direction Allow Multi-Selection (Ctrl+Click) ON Allows selecting multiple nodes by holding Ctrl and clicking Link Snapping OFF Snaps connections to the nearest node when dragging
The MAP tab controls layout and interaction thresholds for the map canvas.
Option Default Unit Description Node Spacing 30 px Minimum spacing between system nodes on auto-layout Drag Threshold 5 px Minimum drag distance before a node move is registered

Action Effect SAVE Persists your settings. They are automatically applied every time your primary character connects. RESET Restores all settings to their factory defaults. CANCEL Closes the dialog without saving any changes. tip Use RESET at any time to return to the default configuration without having to adjust each option manually.

A signature is a point of interest found with probes: a wormhole, or a data, relic, combat, gas or ore site. WHMapper keeps the signatures of each system and shares them live with every pilot on the map, so you know what has already been scanned. When you select a system on the map, its signatures are shown in the Signatures window. This window can be moved, collapsed and resized (see Map panels). With the Signatures window you can: paste the in-game scan results to add or update many signatures at once; see who created or last updated each signature, and when; set the wormhole type of a signature, with its destination class; delete expired signatures, one by one or all at once.

In the game, open the Probe Scanner and select the signatures to copy (Ctrl+A, then Ctrl+C). In WHMapper, check that the right system is selected, then click the import button in the Signatures window. Paste the scan into Scan Result. WHMapper checks the format for every supported EVE language and shows a preview: nothing probed yet: some signatures probed: Click UPDATE SIGNATURES. The signatures appear in the Signatures window: The first pilot to import a signature is its Creator. Each later import or edit of the same signature records the Updater and resets the Updated timer. These timers help you spot old signatures before their wormhole collapses.

The Lazy Deleted option compares your scan with the signatures already saved: Colour Lazy Deleted off (default) Lazy Deleted on Green New signature New signature Grey Updated signature Updated signature Red — Saved signature missing from your scan: it will be deleted Starting from the signatures above, a new scan gives: Lazy Deleted off: Lazy Deleted on: tip The red rows tell you which bookmarks to remove in the game. warning Only turn on Lazy Deleted when you paste all the signatures of the system. With a partial selection, the signatures you did not copy are deleted.

Imports update signatures automatically. You can also edit a signature by hand, for example to set the type of a wormhole: Click the row to edit it. Choose the Group: Set the Type: for a wormhole, choose the wormhole type in the list. Each entry shows the type and its destination class (HS, LS, NS, C1–C6…): for any other group, type free text: Click the pencil to save, or the cross to cancel: Example: a wormhole set to D845 -> HS, about to be saved:
Click the trash icon at the end of the row. Click DELETE to confirm, or CANCEL to keep the signature.
Click the trash icon next to the import button in the table header. Click DELETE to delete every signature of the system, or CANCEL to keep them.

The Statistics module shows who probes and who explores the most on your maps. It helps your corporation recognise the pilots carrying the scanning and scouting effort. The leaderboards are built from WHMapper's own activity history, stored in its database. It shows: Top Probers: pilots ranked by signatures they scanned down or identified. Top Explorers: pilots ranked by systems they opened on a map. Three periods side by side: last 7 days, last 30 days and all time. Filters: by instance and by map. Your own row is highlighted so you can find yourself at a glance.
Open the user menu (⋮ at the top-right of the screen) and click Statistics.

Filter Description Instance The instance to report on. Shown only when you can access more than one instance. Map A single map, or All maps (default). Only activities on maps you are allowed to open are counted, including per-map access restrictions (see Instance → Map Access Control).

The TOP PROBERS tab ranks pilots by the number of signatures they created and updated. Each period shows a stacked bar chart (Created / Updated) and a table. Column Description # Rank Pilot Character name Created New signatures added to a system Updated Existing signatures whose name, group or type changed Total Created + Updated Ties are broken by the number of created signatures.

Signature created: a new signature added by a scan import (paste or Import dialog) from a line at 100% signal strength. Signature updated: an existing signature whose name, group or type changes: by a scan import from a line at 100% signal strength, or by a manual edit that leaves the signature identified (group other than Unknow and type filled in). Signatures probed below 100% are still stored as usual, but they are not counted. Refreshing the scan date of a signature alone is not counted.
The TOP EXPLORERS tab ranks pilots by the number of systems they opened on a map. Each period shows a bar chart and a table.
System opened: each system added to a map where it was not already present, either by automatic location tracking or manually (see Map → Adding Systems).

Each leaderboard shows the Top 10 for three periods displayed side by side: Period Description Last 7 days Rolling window, in UTC Last 30 days Rolling window, in UTC All time Everything recorded since the module was deployed Pilot names are resolved from ESI. When a name cannot be resolved, the character ID is shown instead.

Leaderboards start empty Activity is recorded from the moment WHMapper v3.4.0 is deployed. Past activity is not backfilled, so leaderboards start empty and fill up as your pilots scan and explore. Signature activity is recorded under your primary character (see Authenticate → Multiple Characters). A system opened by location tracking is credited to the character who entered it. Deleting a map or a system does not delete its activity history. Recording never interrupts map operations: if an activity cannot be saved, the map action still completes.

When you select a system on the map, two windows open over the map (see Map panels): System shows what you need to know about the system: location, security, class and, for wormholes, the effect and statics; Notes holds a free-text note about the system, shared with everyone on the map.

The top of the System window links to the selected system on three websites: Link Use it for Dotlan Maps of the region and constellation, jumps and activity zKillboard Recent kills and losses in the system Anoik.is Wormhole details: effect, statics, celestials
The System window shows the region, constellation, name, security status and class of the system.
The security status is colour-coded: Colour Security status Example Red Below 0 (null-sec and wormholes) Orange 0.1 to 0.4 (low-sec) Green 0.5 and above (high-sec)
The class badge tells you what kind of space the system is in. Known space: Class Badge High-sec (HS) Low-sec (LS) Null-sec (NS) Wormhole space: Class Badges C1 to C6 C13 to C18 Thera Pochven
Wormhole systems show two extra lines: Effect and Statics.

Some wormholes have an effect that changes how ships and modules behave. The colour of the square tells you which one: Effect Square Black Hole Cataclysmic Variable Magnetar Pulsar Red Giant Wolf-Rayet Hover the square to see the bonuses and penalties of the effect:
Statics are the wormholes that always spawn in the system. Each one shows its type and its destination class: Hover a static to see its mass limits and lifetime:

The Notes window holds one note per system and per map. Everyone who can open the map sees the same note: use it for what your corporation needs to know about the system (residents, structures, what is inside…).
Click the text area and type. The note is saved automatically a few seconds after you stop typing. A confirmation appears when the note is saved:
Clear the text of the note. The empty note is saved like any other change. info Removing a system from the map does not delete its note. If the system is added again, its note comes back.

EVE-WHMAPPER v1.0.0

EVE Wormhole Mapper (WHMapper) maps wormhole chains for EVE Online pilots and corporations. It tracks where your characters go, draws the chain as you jump, and shares it live with everyone on the map — along with signatures, system information, routes and jump history.
Install your own server: Installation, then First Start. Log in and set up your corporation: Authenticate, then Instance. Use the map: Map, Signature, Route Planner. What's new: Release Notes.
